import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture asks whether every proper minor-closed family of finite graphs has
uniformly bounded distortion into $\ell_1$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, GNRS conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
- [Lee and Sidiropoulos, *Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/

namespace GNRSConjecture

/-- `G` is a graph minor of `H`, expressed by a branch-set model in `H`. -/
def IsMinor {m n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : Fin m → Set (Fin n),
    (∀ i, (H.induce (branch i)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ ⦃i j⦄, i ≠ j → Disjoint (branch i) (branch j)) ∧
    (∀ ⦃i j⦄, G.Adj i j →
      ∃ x ∈ branch i, ∃ y ∈ branch j, H.Adj x y)

/-- A family of finite graphs is minor-closed if it contains every minor of each of its members. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : ∀ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃m n : ℕ⦄ ⦃G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)⦄ ⦃H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)⦄,
    F n H → IsMinor G H → F m G

/-- The weighted shortest-path distance between two vertices, for a nonnegative edge length
function. This is used below only when the vertices are reachable. -/
noncomputable def shortestPathDistance {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (length : Sym2 (Fin n) → ℝ) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  sInf (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u v ↦ (p.edges.map length).sum)

/--
**GNRS conjecture.** For every proper minor-closed family $F$ of finite graphs, there is a
constant $C$, depending only on $F$, such that every shortest-path pseudometric induced by
nonnegative edge lengths on every graph in $F$ embeds into a finite-dimensional $\ell_1$
space with distortion at most $C$. The inequalities are imposed on reachable pairs, so for a
disconnected graph they state the assertion simultaneously on all connected components.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem gnrs_conjecture :
    ∀ F : ∀ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop,
      IsMinorClosed F →
      (∃ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ¬F n G) →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
        ∀ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), F n G →
        ∀ length : Sym2 (Fin n) → ℝ, (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, 0 ≤ length e) →
        ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ f : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ,
          ∀ u v, G.Reachable u v →
            shortestPathDistance G length u v ≤ ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ∧
            ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ≤ C * shortestPathDistance G length u v := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture
modeling_decisions: Represented a family of finite graphs as a dependent predicate `∀ n, SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop`. Minor closure under the branch-set relation also forces invariance under relabeling, so this models ordinary unlabeled graph families without introducing graph quotients.
Encoded “other than the family of all graphs” as the existence of a finite graph outside the family. For a minor-closed family this is equivalent to forbidding some minor.
Used the standard connected, nonempty, pairwise-disjoint branch-set characterization of graph minors because Mathlib has no minor relation for `SimpleGraph`.

Defined weighted shortest-path distance as the infimum of the sums of edge lengths over walks. With nonnegative edge lengths this agrees with the minimum over paths and permits distinct vertices at distance zero.

Imposed embedding inequalities only on reachable vertex pairs. This matches the primary source's convention that disconnected pairs have infinite distance, which cannot be represented in finite-dimensional real ℓ₁; equivalently, the assertion applies simultaneously to all connected components.
Used finite-dimensional functions `Fin k → ℝ` with the explicit sum norm. This suffices for finite pseudometric spaces and avoids requiring an infinite-dimensional ℓ₁ API.
Normalized the non-contraction factor to one: `d ≤ ‖f(u)-f(v)‖₁ ≤ C*d`. This is equivalent to the usual two-scale definition of distortion after rescaling the embedding.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004) states that every
minor-closed family of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs has $\ell_1$
embeddings with bounded distortion: there is a constant $C$, depending only on the family,
such that the shortest-path (pseudo)metric of every graph in the family, for every choice of
nonnegative edge lengths, embeds into $\ell_1$ with distortion at most $C$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
* [GNRS04] Gupta, A., Newman, I., Rabinovich, Y., Sinclair, A. (2004).
  "Cuts, trees and $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs." *Combinatorica* 24 (2), pp. 233--269.
* [LS13] Lee, J. R., Sidiropoulos, A. (2013). "Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings."
  *Combinatorica* 33 (3), pp. 349--374. [arXiv:0910.1409](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/

namespace GNRSConjecture

open SimpleGraph

universe u

variable {V W X : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` says that the simple graph `H` is a *minor* of the simple graph `G`, i.e. `H`
can be obtained from `G` by deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges.

We use the standard equivalent description by *branch sets*: there is a family `A` of pairwise
disjoint, nonempty, connected vertex sets `A w ⊆ V(G)`, indexed by the vertices `w` of `H`, such
that whenever `w` and `w'` are adjacent in `H` there is an edge of `G` between `A w` and `A w'`.
(Contracting each `A w` to a single vertex and deleting everything else yields a graph
containing `H` as a subgraph.) -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (A w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' => Disjoint (A w) (A w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ x ∈ A w, ∃ y ∈ A w', G.Adj x y

/-- Every subgraph of `G` (on the same vertex set) is a minor of `G`; in particular `G` is a
minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {H G : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G := by
  refine ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => ?_, fun v v' hvv' => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hvv', ?_⟩
  · refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    rw [Subsingleton.elim x y]
  · intro w w' hww'
    exact ⟨w, rfl, w', rfl, h hww'⟩

/-- The graph with no vertices is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_empty (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor (⊥ : SimpleGraph Empty) G :=
  ⟨Empty.elim, fun w => w.elim, fun w => w.elim, fun w => w.elim⟩

/-- A family `F` of finite graphs (a predicate on simple graphs with finite vertex type) is
*minor-closed* if every minor of a member of `F` is again a member of `F`.

Since isomorphic graphs are minors of each other, a minor-closed family is in particular
closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : ∀ {V : Type u} [Finite V], SimpleGraph V → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ {V W : Type u} [Finite V] [Finite W] (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W),
    F G → IsMinor H G → F H

/-- The family of all finite graphs is minor-closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinorClosed_top : IsMinorClosed (fun {_ : Type u} [Finite _] _ => True) :=
  fun _ _ _ _ => trivial

/-- The shortest-path pseudometric on the vertices of `G` induced by the edge-length function
`len : Sym2 V → ℝ` (only the values of `len` on edges of `G` matter): `weightedDist G len u v`
is the infimum, over all walks `p` from `u` to `v` in `G`, of the total length of the edges
of `p`.

This is meaningful when `G` is connected and `len` is nonnegative: then the infimum is over a
nonempty set that is bounded below by `0`. It is a pseudometric rather than a metric, since
zero-length edges are allowed. (For unreachable `u`, `v` it takes the junk value `0`, which is
why the conjecture below is restricted to connected graphs.) -/
noncomputable def weightedDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (len : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u v : V) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ p : G.Walk u v, (p.edges.map len).sum

/-- For nonnegative edge lengths, the weighted distance from a vertex to itself is `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem weightedDist_self (G : SimpleGraph V) {len : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hlen : ∀ e, 0 ≤ len e)
    (u : V) : weightedDist G len u u = 0 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · have hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u u => (p.edges.map len).sum) := by
      refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
      rintro _ ⟨p, rfl⟩
      exact List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
        obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hx
        exact hlen e
    simpa using ciInf_le hbdd Walk.nil
  · refine le_ciInf fun p => ?_
    exact List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
      obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hx
      exact hlen e

/-- A pseudometric `d` on `X` *embeds into `ℓ₁` with distortion at most `C`* if there are
`n : ℕ` and a map `f : X → ℝⁿ` such that, measuring distances in `ℝⁿ` with the `ℓ₁`
(sum) norm,
$$d(x, y) \le \|f(x) - f(y)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(x, y)$$
for all `x y : X`.

Since `ℓ₁` distances can be rescaled, this is the same as asking for `c, C' > 0` with
`c * d(x, y) ≤ ‖f(x) - f(y)‖₁ ≤ C' * d(x, y)` and stretch factor `C' / c ≤ C`.
For finite `X`, embeddings into the sequence space `ℓ₁` (or into `L₁`) can be replaced by
embeddings into some finite-dimensional `ℓ₁ⁿ` without changing the distortion. -/
def EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (d : X → X → ℝ) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : X → PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)),
    ∀ x y, d x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y) ∧ dist (f x) (f y) ≤ C * d x y

/-- The real line embeds isometrically into `ℓ₁`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 46]
theorem embedsIntoL1WithDistortion_real :
    EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (fun x y : ℝ => |x - y|) 1 := by
  refine ⟨1, fun x => WithLp.toLp 1 (fun _ => x), fun x y => ?_⟩
  simp [PiLp.dist_eq_sum, Real.dist_eq]

/--
**The GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich, Sinclair, 2004).

Let $\mathcal F$ be a minor-closed family of finite graphs which is not the family of all
finite graphs. Then there is a constant $C = C(\mathcal F)$ such that for every connected
graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function $\mathrm{len}$ on $G$, the
shortest-path pseudometric $d_{\mathrm{len}}$ on $V(G)$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with distortion at
most $C$: there is a map $f : V(G) \to \ell_1$ with
$$d_{\mathrm{len}}(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d_{\mathrm{len}}(u, v)$$
for all vertices $u, v$.

The constant $C$ depends only on the family $\mathcal F$, not on the individual graph or on the
edge lengths. The exclusion of the family of all graphs is essential: expander graphs require
distortion $\Theta(\log n)$. Only connected graphs are considered, since for a disconnected
graph the shortest-path distance between different components is infinite. Equivalently
(by the max-flow/min-cut duality of Linial–London–Rabinovich and GNRS), the multicommodity
flow-cut gap of graphs in $\mathcal F$ is bounded by $C$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 46 68]
theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : ∀ {V : Type u} [Finite V], SimpleGraph V → Prop)
    (hF : IsMinorClosed F) (hF' : ∃ (V : Type u) (_ : Finite V) (G : SimpleGraph V), ¬ F G) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ {V : Type u} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), F G → G.Connected →
      ∀ len : Sym2 V → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 ≤ len e) →
        EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (weightedDist G len) C := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture

modeling_decisions: The terse list entry was expanded using the article and Lee–Sidiropoulos (arXiv:0910.1409): stated in the 'minor-closed family ≠ all graphs' form (as in the article), not the equivalent 'F forbids some minor' form; for minor-closed F these are equivalent, and the equivalence is noted in the docstring of IsMinorClosed.

This is the paper's own 'equivalently' description and standard for finite simple graphs.

A 'family of finite graphs' is a predicate `∀ {V : Type u} [Finite V], SimpleGraph V → Prop` (universe-polymorphic, `Finite` is Prop so proof-irrelevant). Minor-closedness implies isomorphism-invariance because isomorphic graphs are minors of each other. 'Not the family of all graphs' is `∃ V (_ : Finite V) (G : SimpleGraph V), ¬ F G`.
Edge lengths are `len : Sym2 V → ℝ` with `∀ e, 0 ≤ len e`; only the values on edges matter. Zero lengths are allowed, so the induced distance is a pseudometric (as in Lee–Sidiropoulos).

The conjecture is restricted to connected graphs `G.Connected` because for disconnected graphs the shortest-path distance between components is infinite and no finite-distortion embedding exists; this matches the literature's implicit convention (metrics 'supported on G'). An alternative reading (require the inequalities only for reachable pairs) is equivalent in content.

ℓ₁ is modeled as finite-dimensional `PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)` with n existentially quantified per graph (the decomposition notes say this suffices; finite subsets of L₁/ℓ₁ embed isometrically into some ℓ₁ⁿ). Only the forward ('if') direction is stated, as prescribed by the decomposition notes; the converse (families containing all graphs have unbounded distortion, via expanders) is a known theorem and is only mentioned in the docstring. /-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture, named after Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair (2004), asks whether
minor-closed graph families have $\ell_1$ embeddings with bounded distortion. Precisely: for every
minor-closed family $\mathcal F$ of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs, there is a

finite, the target may be taken to be $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the $\ell_1$ (sum) norm for some $n$.

By a theorem of Linial–London–Rabinovich and Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair, the conjecture
is equivalent to the statement that the multicommodity max-flow/min-cut gap of graphs in such a
family is uniformly bounded. Only the metric embedding formulation is stated here. The exclusion of
the family of all graphs is essential: bounded-degree expander graphs on $n$ vertices require
distortion $\Omega(\log n)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
- [GNRS04] Gupta, Anupam; Newman, Ilan; Rabinovich, Yuri; Sinclair, Alistair,
  [*Cuts, trees and $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-004-0015-x),
  Combinatorica 24 (2004), 233--269.
- [LS13] Lee, James R.; Sidiropoulos, Anastasios,
  [*Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409),
  Combinatorica 33 (2013), 349--374.
-/

namespace GNRSConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` is a minor of the graph `G`, in the *minor model*
formulation: every vertex `w` of `H` is assigned a branch set `A w` of vertices of `G` such that
the branch sets are pairwise disjoint, each induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph
of `G`, and every edge `w₁ w₂` of `H` is witnessed by an edge of `G` between `A w₁` and `A w₂`.
This is equivalent to `H` being obtainable from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (A w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (A w₁) (A w₂)) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w₁ w₂⦄, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ A w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ A w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- A family of finite graphs: a predicate on simple graphs with a finite vertex type. -/
abbrev GraphFamily := ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V], SimpleGraph V → Prop

/-- A family of finite graphs is **minor-closed** if every minor of a graph in the family again
belongs to the family. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : GraphFamily) : Prop :=
  ∀ {V W : Type} [Finite V] [Finite W] (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W),
    F G → IsMinor H G → F H

/-- The shortest-path pseudometric on the vertices of `G` induced by the edge-length function
`ℓ`: `pathDist G ℓ u v` is the infimum of the total length $\sum_{e \in p} \ell(e)$ over all walks
`p` from `u` to `v` in `G`. This is the intended quantity when `G` is connected and `ℓ` is
nonnegative; otherwise it may take the junk value `0`. -/
noncomputable def pathDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (ℓ : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u v : V) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ p : G.Walk u v, (p.edges.map ℓ).sum

/-- A pseudometric `d` on `X` **embeds into $\ell_1$ with distortion at most `C`** if there are
`n : ℕ` and a map `f : X → ℝ^n` with
$d(x, y) \le \|f(x) - f(y)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(x, y)$ for all `x y : X`, where
$\|z\|_1 = \sum_i |z_i|$ is the $\ell_1$ norm. -/
def IsL1EmbeddableWithDistortion {X : Type*} (d : X → X → ℝ) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : X → Fin n → ℝ), ∀ x y,
    d x y ≤ ∑ i, |f x i - f y i| ∧ ∑ i, |f x i - f y i| ≤ C * d x y

/-- **GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich, Sinclair, 2004).
Every minor-closed family $\mathcal F$ of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs has
$\ell_1$ embeddings with bounded distortion: there is a constant $C$ (depending on
$\mathcal F$ but not on the individual graphs) such that for every graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and
every nonnegative edge-length function $\ell$ on $G$, the shortest-path pseudometric induced by
$\ell$ on the vertices of $G$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with distortion at most $C$.

The shortest-path pseudometric is only finite-valued on connected graphs, so the statement
ranges over the connected members of $\mathcal F$. This loses nothing: every connected
component of a graph in a minor-closed family belongs to the family. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 46]
theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : GraphFamily) (hF : IsMinorClosed F)
    (hF' : ¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), F G) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), F G → G.Connected →
      ∀ ℓ : Sym2 V → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 ≤ ℓ e) →
        IsL1EmbeddableWithDistortion (pathDist G ℓ) C := by
  sorry

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G := by
  refine ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => Connected.of_subsingleton, fun v w hvw => ?_,
    fun v w h => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h⟩⟩
  exact Set.disjoint_singleton.2 hvw

/-- A subgraph of `G` (on the same vertex set) is a minor of `G`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_of_le {H G : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G := by
  refine ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => Connected.of_subsingleton, fun v w hvw => ?_,
    fun v w hvw => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h hvw⟩⟩
  exact Set.disjoint_singleton.2 hvw

/-- The shortest-path pseudometric is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem pathDist_nonneg (G : SimpleGraph V) {ℓ : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hℓ : ∀ e, 0 ≤ ℓ e) (u v : V) :
    0 ≤ pathDist G ℓ u v :=
  Real.iInf_nonneg fun p => List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
    obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
    exact hℓ e

/-- The shortest-path pseudometric vanishes on the diagonal for nonnegative edge lengths. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem pathDist_self (G : SimpleGraph V) {ℓ : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hℓ : ∀ e, 0 ≤ ℓ e) (u : V) :
    pathDist G ℓ u u = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (pathDist_nonneg G hℓ u u)
  have hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u u => (p.edges.map ℓ).sum) := by
    refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
    rintro x ⟨p, rfl⟩
    exact List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
      obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
      exact hℓ e
  simpa using ciInf_le hbdd (Walk.nil : G.Walk u u)

/-- The real line embeds isometrically into $\ell_1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 46]
theorem isL1EmbeddableWithDistortion_abs_sub :
    IsL1EmbeddableWithDistortion (fun x y : ℝ => |x - y|) 1 :=
  ⟨1, fun x _ => x, fun x y => by simp⟩

end GNRSConjecture

Isomorphism-closure is not assumed separately because minor-closedness (with the minor-model definition) implies it: isomorphic graphs are minors of each other.

'Other than the family of all graphs' is formalized literally as `¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), F G`. For a minor-closed family this is equivalent to 'F forbids some minor' (the phrasing in Lee–Sidiropoulos).

/-- The extended shortest-path distance associated to nonnegative edge lengths.
Lengths assigned to nonedges are ignored. -/
noncomputable def weightedEDist {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (length : Sym2 V → NNReal) (u v : V) : ENNReal :=

    (↑(w.edges.map length).sum : ENNReal))

/-- `H` is a graph minor of `G`, expressed using disjoint connected branch sets. -/
def IsGraphMinor {U V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph U) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : U → Finset V,
    (∀ u, (branch u).Nonempty ∧ (G.induce (branch u : Set V)).Preconnected) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄, u ≠ v → Disjoint (branch u) (branch v)) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v →
      ∃ x ∈ branch u, ∃ y ∈ branch v, G.Adj x y)

/--

constant $C=C(\mathcal F)$ such that, for every $G\in\mathcal F$ and every nonnegative
edge-length function, the induced shortest-path pseudometric on each connected component of
$G$ embeds into some finite-dimensional $\ell_1$ with distortion at most $C$. The constant is
independent of the graph and its edge lengths. Here all finite graphs are represented, up to
isomorphism, as graphs on `Fin n`, and edge lengths are extended arbitrarily to nonedges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem gnrs_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ F : (n : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop,
      (∀ {m n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)},
        IsGraphMinor H G → F n G → F m H) →
      (∃ n, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ¬ F n G) →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
        ∀ {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), F n G →
          ∀ length : Sym2 (Fin n) → NNReal,
            ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ f : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ,
              ∀ u v, G.Reachable u v →
                (weightedEDist G length u v).toReal ≤
                    ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ∧
                  ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ≤
                    C * (weightedEDist G length u v).toReal := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture

has bounded $\ell_1$ distortion: there is a constant $C$, depending only on the family, such that
for every graph in the family and every non-negative length function on its edges, the induced
shortest-path (pseudo)metric on the vertices embeds into $\ell_1$ with distortion at most $C$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
- [GNRS04] Gupta, A., Newman, I., Rabinovich, Y., Sinclair, A. (2004). "Cuts, trees and
  $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs." *Combinatorica* 24 (2), pp. 233--269.
- [LS09] Lee, J. R., Sidiropoulos, A. (2009). "Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings."
  [arXiv:0910.1409](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/

open SimpleGraph NNReal

namespace GNRSConjecture

variable {V W X : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` means that `H` is a minor of `G`, i.e. `H` can be obtained from `G` by
deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges. We use the standard equivalent
formulation via *branch sets*: there is a family `φ` of pairwise disjoint vertex subsets of `G`,
indexed by the vertices of `H`, each inducing a connected (in particular non-empty) subgraph of
`G`, such that for every edge `w w'` of `H` there is an edge of `G` between `φ w` and `φ w'`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (φ w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' => Disjoint (φ w) (φ w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ φ w, ∃ v ∈ φ w', G.Adj u v

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun _ => Connected.of_subsingleton,
    fun _ _ h => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr h,
    fun u v huv => ⟨u, rfl, v, rfl, huv⟩⟩

/-- A family `F` of finite graphs is *minor-closed* if it contains every minor of each of its
members. Families are represented as sets of graphs on the vertex sets `Fin n`. Since a graph is
a minor of every graph isomorphic to it, a minor-closed family is closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : Set (Σ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ G ∈ F, ∀ H : Σ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsMinor H.2 G.2 → H ∈ F

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinorClosed_univ : IsMinorClosed Set.univ := fun _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

/-- The shortest-path distance between `u` and `v` in `G` with respect to the non-negative
edge-length function `len`: the infimum of the total length of all walks from `u` to `v`.
Values of `len` on non-edges are irrelevant. If `u` and `v` are not reachable from one another,
this takes the junk value `0`; the conjecture below is therefore only stated for connected graphs
(which loses no generality, since a minor-closed family contains the connected components of its
members). -/
noncomputable def weightedDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (len : Sym2 V → ℝ≥0) (u v : V) :

theorem weightedDist_self (G : SimpleGraph V) (len : Sym2 V → ℝ≥0) (u : V) :

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004) states that every minor-closed
family of finite graphs, other than the family of all graphs, has $\ell_1$ embeddings with bounded
distortion: there is a constant $C$, depending only on the family, such that the shortest-path
metric of every graph in the family, with respect to every nonnegative edge-length function,
embeds into an $\ell_1$ space with distortion at most $C$.

Equivalently (Linial–London–Rabinovich, GNRS), the multi-commodity max-flow/min-cut gap of
graphs in a minor-closed family is uniformly bounded. We formalise the metric embedding
formulation.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [GNRS04] Gupta, A., Newman, I., Rabinovich, Y., Sinclair, A. (2004). "Cuts, trees and
  $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs." *Combinatorica* 24 (2), pp. 233--269.
* [LS13] Lee, J. R., Sidiropoulos, A. (2013). "Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings."
  *Combinatorica* 33 (3), pp. 349--374. [arXiv:0910.1409](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace GNRSConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/- ## Graph minors -/

/-- `IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` is a minor of the graph `G`: there is a partial map
`φ` from the vertices of `G` to the vertices of `H` (`φ v = none` means that `v` is deleted) whose
fibres (the *branch sets*) are nonempty and induce connected subgraphs of `G`, and such that every
edge of `H` is realised by an edge of `G` between the corresponding branch sets. Contracting each
branch set to a single vertex and deleting the remaining vertices and edges then yields `H`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : V → Option W,
    (∀ w : W, (G.induce {v | φ v = some w}).Connected) ∧
    ∀ a b : W, H.Adj a b → ∃ u v : V, φ u = some a ∧ φ v = some b ∧ G.Adj u v

/-- Every subgraph of `G` (on the same vertex set) is a minor of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma IsMinor.of_le {G H : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G := by
  refine ⟨some, fun w => ?_, fun a b hab => ⟨a, b, rfl, rfl, h hab⟩⟩
  have : Subsingleton {v | some v = some w} := ⟨fun ⟨x, hx⟩ ⟨y, hy⟩ => by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Option.some.injEq] at hx hy
    exact Subtype.ext (hx.trans hy.symm)⟩
  have : Nonempty {v | some v = some w} := ⟨⟨w, rfl⟩⟩
  exact Connected.of_subsingleton

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G := .of_le le_rfl

/-- The one-vertex graph is a minor of every connected graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isMinor_bot_unit (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) :
    IsMinor (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) G := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => some (), fun _ => ?_, fun a b hab => absurd hab (by simp)⟩
  have hs : {v : V | (some () : Option Unit) = some ()} = Set.univ := by ext; simp
  rw [hs]
  exact (induceUnivIso G).connected_iff.mpr hG

/- ## Shortest-path metrics and `ℓ₁` embeddings -/

/-- The length of a walk `p` in a graph with edge-length function `w`: the sum of the lengths of
the edges traversed by `p` (counted with multiplicity). -/
def walkLength {G : SimpleGraph V} (w : Sym2 V → ℝ) {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v) : ℝ :=
  (p.edges.map w).sum

/-- The shortest-path distance between `u` and `v` in the graph `G` with respect to the edge-length
function `w`: the infimum of the lengths of all walks from `u` to `v`. For nonnegative `w` and a
connected graph `G`, this is the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ *supported on* `G`.
(For vertices in different components the set of walks is empty and `sInf ∅ = 0`, so this
definition is only meaningful for connected graphs.) -/
noncomputable def shortestPathDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u v : V) : ℝ :=
  sInf (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u v => walkLength w p)

/-- The trivial walk has length `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma walkLength_nil {G : SimpleGraph V} (w : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u : V) :
    walkLength w (Walk.nil : G.Walk u u) = 0 := by
  simp [walkLength]

/-- A pseudometric `d` on `V` *embeds into `ℓ₁` with distortion at most `C`* if there is a map
`f` from `V` to a finite-dimensional real vector space with the `ℓ₁` (sum) norm such that
$d(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(u, v)$ for all `u v`. Since a finite subset of any
$L_1$ space embeds isometrically into $\ell_1^n$ for some $n$, and the distortion is invariant
under rescaling `f`, this agrees with the usual notion of $\ell_1$-distortion at most `C` for
pseudometrics on finite sets. -/
def EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (d : V → V → ℝ) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : V → PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)),
    ∀ u v : V, d u v ≤ dist (f u) (f v) ∧ dist (f u) (f v) ≤ C * d u v

/- ## The conjecture -/

/--
**The GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004).

Let $\mathcal F$ be a minor-closed family of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs
(equivalently, $\mathcal F$ forbids some minor). Then there is a constant $C = C(\mathcal F)$ such
that for every (connected) graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function
$w$ on $G$, the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ on the vertices of $G$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with
distortion at most $C$; that is, there is a map $f$ from the vertices of $G$ into an $\ell_1$ space
with $d_w(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d_w(u, v)$ for all vertices $u, v$.

Here a family of finite graphs is given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex set `Fin n`.
The conclusion is only asserted for connected members of the family since the shortest-path
metric of a disconnected graph takes infinite values; this loses nothing, as the connected
components of members of a minor-closed family belong to the family.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 46]
theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n)))
    (hF : ∀ {n m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)),
      G ∈ F n → IsMinor H G → H ∈ F m)
    (hF' : ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ F n) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.Connected →
      ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin n) → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 ≤ w e) →
        EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (shortestPathDist G w) C := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture

The GNRS conjecture concerns embeddings of shortest-path metrics of weighted finite graphs into
$\ell_1$, uniformly over a proper minor-closed family of graphs.

- [Wikipedia, *GNRS conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
- [J. R. Lee and A. Sidiropoulos, *Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)

namespace GNRSConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
`H` is a graph minor of `G`, expressed by the standard branch-set characterization: the vertices
of `H` are represented by pairwise disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets of `G`, and every edge
of `H` is represented by an edge of `G` between the corresponding sets.
-/
def IsMinor {m n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : Fin m → Set (Fin n),
    (∀ i, (G.induce (branch i)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (branch i) (branch j)) ∧
    ∀ ⦃i j⦄, H.Adj i j → ∃ u ∈ branch i, ∃ v ∈ branch j, G.Adj u v

/--
The shortest-path pseudodistance induced by nonnegative edge lengths. The length of a walk counts
edges with multiplicity, and the distance is the infimum of the lengths of all walks between the
two vertices.
-/
noncomputable def weightedDist {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (length : G.edgeSet → NNReal) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  sInf (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u v ↦
    (p.darts.map fun d ↦ (length ⟨d.edge, d.edge_mem⟩ : ℝ)).sum)

/--
**GNRS conjecture.** For every proper minor-closed family $\mathcal F$ of finite graphs, there is
a constant $C$, depending only on $\mathcal F$, such that every shortest-path pseudometric induced
by nonnegative edge lengths on a connected graph $G \in \mathcal F$ has a noncontracting embedding
into a finite-dimensional $\ell_1$ space whose Lipschitz constant is at most $C$. Thus its
distortion is at most $C$, independently of the graph, its edge lengths, and the target dimension.

Here a family is represented by its members on each labeled vertex type `Fin n`. Properness means
that it is not the family of all finite graphs. Restricting to connected graphs is the usual
shortest-path pseudometric convention; disconnected graphs are handled componentwise.
-/

theorem gnrs_conjecture :
    ∀ family : (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      (∀ {m n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)},
        G ∈ family n → IsMinor H G → H ∈ family m) →
      (∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ family n) →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
        ∀ {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ family n → G.Connected →
          ∀ length : G.edgeSet → NNReal,
            ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ f : Fin n → PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin k ↦ ℝ),
              ∀ u v, weightedDist G length u v ≤ dist (f u) (f v) ∧

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture asks whether every proper minor-closed family of finite graphs has uniformly
bounded distortion in $\ell_1$.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, GNRS conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
-/

namespace GNRSConjecture

open scoped Sym2
open SimpleGraph

/-- The length of a walk when each (undirected) edge has a nonnegative real length. -/
def walkLength {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (w : Sym2 V → NNReal) :
    {u v : V} → G.Walk u v → NNReal
  | _, _, .nil => 0
  | u, _, .cons (v := v) _ p => w s(u, v) + walkLength w p

/-- The weighted shortest-path distance between two vertices. This is used only for reachable
pairs below, so the set whose infimum is taken is nonempty. -/
noncomputable def weightedDist {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 V → NNReal)
    (u v : V) : NNReal :=
  sInf {r | ∃ p : G.Walk u v, walkLength w p = r}

/-- `H` is a minor of `G` if the vertices of `H` admit pairwise disjoint, nonempty, connected
branch sets in `G`, with adjacent branch sets for every edge of `H`. -/
def IsMinor {V W : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph V) (G : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : V → Set W,
    (∀ v, (branch v).Nonempty ∧ (G.induce (branch v)).Preconnected) ∧
    (Set.univ : Set V).PairwiseDisjoint branch ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v → ∃ x ∈ branch u, ∃ y ∈ branch v, G.Adj x y

/-- A common type containing one representative `SimpleGraph (Fin n)` for each size `n`. -/
abbrev FiniteGraph := Σ n : ℕ, SimpleGraph (Fin n)

/-- A family of finite graphs is minor-closed if it contains every minor of each of its members. -/
def MinorClosed (F : Set FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃H G : FiniteGraph⦄, IsMinor H.2 G.2 → G ∈ F → H ∈ F

/--
**GNRS conjecture.** For every proper minor-closed family $F$ of finite graphs, there is a
constant $C=C(F)$ such that, for every $G\in F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function, the
induced shortest-path pseudometric on each connected component of $G$ embeds in a
finite-dimensional $\ell_1$ space with distortion at most $C$. The constant is independent of
$G$ and of the edge lengths. The inequalities use the equivalent normalization in which the
embedding is non-contracting. Pairs in different connected components, whose shortest-path
distance is infinite, impose no condition.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 05 51]
theorem gnrs_conjecture :
    ∀ F : Set FiniteGraph, MinorClosed F → F ≠ Set.univ →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), (⟨n, G⟩ : FiniteGraph) ∈ F →
          ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin n) → NNReal,
            ∃ (k : ℕ) (f : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ), ∀ u v, G.Reachable u v →
              (weightedDist G w u v : ℝ) ≤ ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ∧
                ∑ i, |f u i - f v i| ≤ C * weightedDist G w u v := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture
modeling_decisions: Represented finite graphs canonically as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)` packaged in a sigma type. A family is proper when it is not `Set.univ`; together with minor closure this is equivalent to forbidding some finite graph minor.
Defined graph minor by the standard branch-set characterization: nonempty connected pairwise-disjoint branch sets, with a cross-edge for every edge of the minor graph.

Represented a nonnegative undirected edge-length function as `Sym2 (Fin n) → NNReal`. Although this function is defined on all unordered vertex pairs, only its values on graph edges are read by `walkLength`, so this is equivalent to a function on the edge set while avoiding dependent edge-subtype bookkeeping.

Defined weighted shortest-path distance as the infimum of lengths of graph walks. Distortion inequalities are required for reachable pairs. Thus, for a disconnected graph, the statement simultaneously embeds the shortest-path pseudometrics of its connected components and imposes no condition on pairs at infinite extended distance, matching the primary source's convention.
Used finite-dimensional coordinate spaces `Fin k → ℝ` and wrote their ℓ₁ distance explicitly as `∑ i, |f u i - f v i|`. This avoids accidentally using Mathlib's default sup norm on function spaces.
Normalized each embedding to be non-contracting, with `d ≤ ‖f(u)-f(v)‖₁ ≤ C*d`. This is equivalent to the source's two-scale-factor definition of distortion after rescaling.

Did not require the map to be injective, because zero edge lengths are allowed and the induced object is a pseudometric; the lower inequality supplies the appropriate metric-quotient notion of embedding.
